items.title: Ongoing work will extend life of sanitary sewer on major Mississauga road
items.summary: Peel Region crews are completing major sewer work on a main street in Mississauga’s north end that will disrupt local traffic until the job is finished. Project leaders said in a recent update the region is rehabilitating the sanitary sewer along Falconer Drive, located in the Streetsville area of the city. Work got underway in October and is expected to continue until close to the end of the year, the region said. Timelines may change due to weather and other unexpected events, officials added. “Sanitary sewers are underground pipes that carry wastewater from your home to a water resource recovery facility. Wastewater is created when water goes down a drain or toilet,” project officials said in a notice to area residents and businesses. “We’ll clean the sewer pipe and place a new resin (plastic) lining inside to extend its life. , under contract to Peel Region. m. , Monday to Friday, the region noted, adding the schedule is intended to shorten the construction period. Map shows Falconer Drive in Mississauga where sanitary sewer upgrades are being completed. During the work period, project leaders say they may need to temporarily reduce traffic to a single lane on the busy street.

items.title: VIDEO: Hero truck driver from Mississauga honoured after daring highway rescue
items.summary: A Mississauga truck driver who risked his own life to pull a woman from a burning vehicle during a massive winter highway pileup is being recognized for his extraordinary bravery. Isik Altinisik has been named the recipient of this year’s Ontario Trucking Association-Bridgestone Truck Hero Award after helping rescue motorists caught in a devastating multi-vehicle collision on Highway 401 near Trenton earlier this year. Altinisik was making a delivery of fresh food products to Ottawa on Jan. 27 when he encountered the collision amid blinding snow and whiteout conditions. The chain-reaction crashes involved approximately 50 vehicles across a stretch of Highway 401 in eastern Ontario, with one of the worst incidents involving a 17-vehicle pileup near Trenton. Rather than continuing on his way, Altinisik rushed toward the wreckage to help those in danger. Among the people trapped in the chaos was Theresa Rozendaal, whose SUV had been involved in a collision and was beginning to catch fire. With flames emerging from beneath the hood and her windshield shattered, Rozendaal was in serious danger. Altinisik broke the rear window of her vehicle with his bare hands, injuring himself in the process, before pulling her from the wreckage and getting her to safety in another vehicle.

items.title: Foul odour will nearly disappear once Mississauga wastewater plant is modernized: Region
items.summary: Southeast Mississauga residents who have dealt with foul odours for decades near a large wastewater treatment plant are being told the on-and-off smells will nearly disappear once the 71-year-old facility is modernized. E. Booth Water Resource Recovery Facility, formerly the Lakeview Wastewater Treatment Plant. E. Booth is being upgraded to reduce odours and modernize the facility. The local community can expect odours to drop by more than 90 per cent once this work is done,” Peel Region said in an online description of the odour-removal efforts, which are on track for completion in 2027. Officials said earlier that approximately half of the odour mitigation program is scheduled to be completed by end of 2026, with the bulk of the work being completed in 2027. Officials added the region is committed to reducing odours related to the wastewater collection and treatment process by: The upgrades are being made to address the city and Peel’s continued population growth, in particular the huge Lakeview Village development in Mississauga’s southeast corner that’s bringing some 16,000 new homes to the area. E. Booth facility is the largest wastewater treatment plant in Peel and is designed to treat municipal wastewater from residential, commercial and industrial customers. Serving east Mississauga, east Brampton and part of York Region, it has undergone multiple expansions over the years and currently has a capacity of 518 million litres per day, region officials said.

items.title: 'There's no jet lag to play cricket' — how Ranil Mendis went from new immigrant to Mississauga's 2026 citizen of the year
items.summary: Cricket helped Ranil Mendis find community as a new immigrant. What he gave back earned him Mississauga’s citizen of the year award. School cricket advocate and philanthropist Ranil Mendis was presented Mississauga’s Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year on Nov. 4. Cricket advocate and philanthropist Ranil Mendis has been named Mississauga’s 2026 citizen of the year. Mendis was presented the 2026 Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year by Mississauga Deputy Mayor Matt Mahoney on Nov. 4 at the city’s annual Civic Recognition awards event. A key figure in the Mississauga and Ontario cricket scene, Mendis was recognized for his leadership, community service, philanthropy and ability to inspire others, according to a City of Mississauga news release. “Mississauga is a great city because of the people who give back, and Ranil Mendis is one of those people,” Mahoney said in the release. ” A board member with the Ontario School Cricket Association (OSCA), Mendis helped bring the Mayor’s School Cricket Program to Mississauga and the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants Schools Cricket Program to several Ontario school boards.

items.title: El Niño to bring milder temperatures, and more potholes, to Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials say a potentially historic El Niño that’s expected to bring milder temperatures to southern Ontario this fall and winter will also impact the city in other ways. Coupled with climate change, “which is warming ocean waters,” the El Niño effect could be even stronger, the City of Mississauga said this week. “In Mississauga, that could mean a slower start to winter and more days when temperatures rise above and fall below freezing,” city officials said Thursday, adding some city services “may be delayed or look different than usual” as a result. “A strong El Niño could bring a longer, milder fall and a higher chance of extreme weather to Mississauga,” the city continued. Beyond Mississauga and southern Ontario, weather experts have said El Niño, a natural weather pattern caused by warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures that can affect global weather, will also have a strong impact across much of Canada in the coming months. ” Residents should become familiar with the municipality’s online emergency preparedness guide, officials added.

items.title: Jamal Francique Inquest Delayed to Friday, Nearly Seven Years After Mississauga Police Shooting
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique has been postponed by a day and will now begin Friday instead of Thursday. The outlet reported a notice on the inquest's website said further details on the delay would be provided then. Francique died in hospital on Jan. 9, 2020, two days after Peel Regional Police shot him during an attempted arrest in Mississauga; he was 28, insauga.com said. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit cleared the officers of wrongdoing about a year later, saying the officer who fired reported fearing for his life after Francique drove toward him, according to the report. The SIU noted it still had questions about the officer's decision to position himself near the fleeing vehicle, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Canada-Wide Warrant Ends as Mississauga Double-Shooting Suspect Turns Himself In
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a man wanted on a Canada-wide warrant in connection with a double shooting earlier this year in Mississauga has turned himself in to detectives. According to insauga.com, Carlos Rodriguez-Rodriguez, 22, of Mississauga, surrendered to police on Nov. 9 after returning to the country; officers did not say where he had been. The outlet reported Rodriguez-Rodriguez faces multiple charges tied to a Feb. 21 shooting at a plaza near Kennedy Road and Eglinton Avenue East. Detectives from Peel police's 12 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau identified him as a suspect in the months after the shooting, insauga.com said. Police issued the Canada-wide warrant for his arrest in May, after investigators determined he had left the country following the February shooting, according to the report.

items.title: Mon Gat'ô Pâtisserie Trades Port Credit Storefront for Streetsville Space
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mon Gat'ô Pâtisserie has closed its Port Credit shop at 150 Lakeshore Rd. W. and reopened at a new address in Streetsville. The outlet reported the bakery, known for coffee, pastries, gourmet cookies and cakes, announced the move on Instagram last week. Mon Gat'ô thanked its Port Credit customers in the post, saying the community had welcomed and supported the business, insauga.com said. The bakery's new home is at 237 Queen St. S., a space previously occupied by Streetsville Travel and briefly by a juice and coffee shop, according to the report. Its former Port Credit location, insauga.com noted, had been home to a La Diperie ice cream and desserts shop before Mon Gat'ô moved in.

items.title: Winning Mississauga Lotto 6/49 Gold Ball ticket worth $38M: OLG
items.summary: A winning Lotto 6/49 Gold Ball ticket sold in Mississauga is worth $38 million, the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation (OLG) says. The ticket was from Wednesday’s draw, the OLG said. A winning ticket for the Lotto 6/49 Second Prize worth $211,077 was bought in Toronto. Furthermore, a $1-million Encore ticket was sold in the Leeds and Grenville region. Lotto 6/49 jackpots are every Wednesday and Saturday.

items.title: Coroner's inquest to examine police-involved shooting death of Mississauga man
items.summary: A coroner's inquest, initially set for Thursday, will begin on Friday to examine the circumstances surrounding the death of a man who was shot in the head by police west of Toronto nearly seven years ago.

items.title: OLG Confirms $38-Million Gold Ball Jackpot Ticket Sold in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, a Lotto 6/49 ticket sold in Mississauga has won the $38-million Gold Ball jackpot from Wednesday night's draw. The outlet reported the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation said the winning ticket was purchased in Mississauga, making it one of the province's largest lottery wins this year. The Nov. 11 draw also produced other sizable prizes across Ontario, CityNews said, including a $1-million Encore prize won by a ticket sold in the Leeds and Grenville region. The identity of the $38-million winner has not yet been released, according to the report. CityNews noted that lottery winners must have their tickets validated through OLG before any prize can be officially awarded.

items.title: City Warns Milder El Niño Winter Could Delay Mississauga's Outdoor Ice Rinks
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a strong El Niño pattern could bring a longer, milder fall and a greater chance of extreme weather to the city this year. The city said El Niño is driven by warmer than normal ocean temperatures and that climate change may be intensifying its effects. Mississauga could see a slower start to winter with more freeze-thaw days, which the city said may delay or alter some services. The city operates four artificial outdoor rinks, and warmer temperatures make it harder to form and maintain ice on them, according to the city. Mississauga said it may delay or pause rink openings for safety reasons and urged residents to call 905-615-3200 ext. RINK or check signage at natural, volunteer-run rinks before heading out. The city also warned that repeated freezing and thawing can weaken trees and cause branches to fall.
